guideTitle: 5 Best Mildew Resistant Bath Mats in 2026
metaTitle: Best Mildew Resistant Bath Mats in 2026
metaDescription: Five non slip bath mats built to resist mildew compared by drainage, hang-to-dry hooks, cleaning instructions and what actually stops mold under a suction mat.
mainKeyword: non slip bath mat mildew resistant
introParagraphs: Mildew on a bath mat is almost never about the material alone. It grows where moisture sits: in the soap film between the suction cups, in the trapped water under a mat that lies flat all day and in the pockets of a surface that never fully dries. A mat labelled mildew resistant can help, but the habits around it do most of the work, and the best design is one that makes those habits easy.

The five mats here are the homerella 35 by 16 inch mat with an anti-mold and mildew resistant design and over 250 suction cups, the homerella kids version at 40 by 16 inches with two self-adhesive hooks for hanging, the OTHWAY with 198 cups and 360 drain holes, the TEESHLY 40 by 16 inch mat with drain holes and the GORILLA GRIP 35 by 16 inch mat with hundreds of drainage holes and a BPA-free build.

We evaluated each on drainage, how easy it is to hang and dry, cleaning instructions and what the listing claims about mildew. Resistance claims are the makers' wording and no mat is immune, so we focus on the features that reduce the moisture mildew needs, and on the routine that keeps any mat fresh. Think of the claim on the box as a starting point and the drying routine as the real protection.

products.name: homerella Bathtub Mat, 35x16, Anti Mold, Over 250 Cups
products.description:
homerella puts mildew resistance in the product description and backs it with extra large drain holes, a machine-washable-on-cold instruction and an odorless material. At 35 by 16 inches with over 250 suction cups, it is a standard tub mat built around keeping water moving and making cleaning easy. The listing calls the mat antibacterial, which is the maker's wording.

Large drain holes keep water from standing under the mat, and a cold machine wash clears the soap film that mildew feeds on. The instruction to use cold is the kind of detail that makes the difference between a mat that lasts and one that warps. The listing does not give a hole count in the text we have.

Compared with the kids version it is a plain adult tub mat, and compared with the OTHWAY it gives a wash instruction rather than hole numbers. It suits a household that wants a straightforward mat with a clear cleaning routine. If you ever see dark spots on the underside, wash it promptly on cold and let it dry fully before the next use, because a mat that stays damp will bloom again within days. A second mat in rotation makes this much easier to manage. A new mat should be rinsed and left to air out before first use.
products.bestFor: A standard tub mat with a clear cold-wash routine.
pros: Mold and mildew resistant design, per the listing
cons: Antibacterial wording is the maker's claim
Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: homerella Kids Bathtub Mat, 40x16, Anti Mold, Hooks Included
products.description:
This is the mat with the feature that most directly attacks mildew: two self-adhesive hooks in the box, so you can hang the mat after every use instead of leaving it flat. The listing calls the hooks the secret to its extra durable anti-mold design, and describes a 40 by 16 inch mat with more than 200 suction cups, a BPA-free, non-toxic build and a colorful ocean-animal pattern for children. The kids theme is the most obvious difference from the adult mats.

Hanging a mat so that air reaches both sides is the single most effective anti-mildew habit, and including the hooks makes it effortless. The 40-inch length covers a long tub. The ocean-animal pattern appeals to children and may not suit every adult household, and the listing does not state a drain hole count in the text we have.

Compared with the adult homerella it adds the hooks and the length, and compared with the TEESHLY it states a cup count. It suits a family with children that wants a mat that hangs itself up. The adhesive hooks are best placed at a height where the mat hangs clear of the tub, so that drips fall into the tub and not onto the floor. Check them every few weeks, since a hook that lets go in the night leaves a wet mat on the bathroom floor.
products.bestFor: Families who want a mat that hangs to dry after every bath.
pros: Two self-adhesive hooks included for hanging
40 by 16 in covers a long tub

products.name: OTHWAY Non Slip Bath Tub Shower Mat, 198 Cups, 360 Drain Holes
products.description:
OTHWAY's pitch is drainage: 360 precision-angled holes compared with 250 on what it calls standard mats, which the listing says accelerate water removal. It adds 198 high-density suction cups, a flexible TPE body and raised nodules. Faster drainage means less standing water, and less standing water means less for mildew to use.

TPE is a closed, smooth material that does not soak up water the way a fabric or foam would, which helps it dry. The listing does not make an explicit mildew claim in the text we have, so we read the drain count as the relevant feature. Dimensions are not given in the text.

Compared with the homerella it states a drain count but gives no mildew language, and compared with the GORILLA GRIP it states both counts. It suits a buyer who wants proof of drainage and will handle the cleaning routine. Because TPE does not absorb water, a quick shake and a hang is often all it needs. Run a thumb along the drain holes once a week to push out any hair or soap film that has built up inside them. The nodules also keep the mat's top slightly raised so that water drains rather than pooling.
products.bestFor: A mat whose drainage is backed by a stated hole count.
pros: Flexible TPE does not soak up water
cons: No explicit mildew claim in the text we have
Dimensions are not stated in the text we have

products.name: TEESHLY Bath Tub and Shower Mat, 40 x 16 Inch, Machine Washable
products.description:
TEESHLY's long mat is made of soft-touch PVC with a domed, pebble-like top and drain holes, and is machine washable. The listing does not speak about mildew in the text we have, but the features that matter are there: drainage, a smooth material and washability. At 40 by 16 inches it covers a long tub, and a longer mat has more surface to dry.

Machine washing is a good defense against mildew because it removes the film between the cups. A longer mat takes more effort to dry, so hanging it over the tub edge or a rod is worth the habit. The listing does not give a cup count in the text we have.

Compared with the homerella kids mat it has no hooks, and compared with the OTHWAY it is longer and PVC. It suits a long tub where the owner will wash and hang the mat regularly. A longer mat has more area to dry, so choose a hanging spot with room for all 40 inches, such as a shower rod or the tub edge. Fold it over a bar with the cups facing outward so air reaches the grimiest side. Because it is washable, you can launder it as part of your regular towel routine.

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Bath Tub Shower Mat, 35x16 Clear, Machine Washable
products.description:
GORILLA GRIP offers a washable mat with hundreds of drainage holes that the listing says let water flow easily under the mat toward the drain, helping to prevent water from sitting. It has hundreds of suction cups, a BPA-free pebble-textured top and a standard 35 by 16 inch size. The anti-stagnation wording is the closest the listing comes to a mildew claim.

As a clear mat it will show grime and discoloration plainly, which is useful: you see when it needs washing. The listing does not state a cup count or a wash temperature in the text we have. A cold, gentle cycle is the safest default.

Compared with the homerella it gives less care guidance, and compared with the OTHWAY it gives no hole count. It suits a buyer who wants a well-known washable mat and will follow a good drying routine. The clear finish is an advantage here, because mildew shows as darkening that you can spot early. Wash it at the first sign and rinse the underside by hand between washes. If your tub is stained, a clear mat will show it, so rinse the tub floor with the mat lifted.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Mildew grows where moisture and soap film sit, so the best defense is to keep the mat dry between showers. Look for drainage, a smooth non-absorbent material and a way to hang the mat. A mat that dries in a few hours resists mildew far better than one that stays damp overnight. The resistance claim matters less than the drying. Notice how long your own bathroom takes to dry after a shower, since a damp, windowless room needs a mat that dries faster.

The homerella kids mat includes two self-adhesive hooks so that the mat hangs after every bath. Others can be draped over the tub edge or a rod. A mat that is easy to hang gets hung. Check that your wall can take adhesive hooks. Use the ventilation fan or open a window for twenty minutes after a shower, which helps any mat stay dry.

The OTHWAY lists 360 holes, the GORILLA GRIP hundreds and the homerella extra large holes. More and larger holes move water off the floor and out from under the mat. Drainage reduces standing water. Hair and soap film can block holes, so rinse them. Look at the underside of the mat, because the cups and holes are where mildew starts and where you should clean first.

The homerella says machine wash on cold, and the TEESHLY and GORILLA GRIP say machine washable. A regular wash removes the film between the cups. Use a cold, gentle cycle, a mesh bag and air drying, and skip bleach. A mat that is washed rarely will grow mildew whatever the label says. Wash on a cold, gentle cycle with mild detergent, and skip bleach, which can leave a film that traps grime.

TPE on the OTHWAY and soft PVC on the TEESHLY are non-absorbent, and the homerella is described as odorless. Absorbent foams hold more water. Rinse a new mat to reduce smell. An odor that returns after washing is a sign to replace the mat. Keep a spare mat if mildew has been a repeat problem, so that one can dry completely while the other is in use.

All five use suction cups, which need a smooth, non-porous tub floor. Lifting the mat after each shower lets the tub floor dry too, which matters as much as drying the mat. A damp floor under a flat mat is where mildew starts. Lift the mat and wipe the tub floor with a cloth after each shower, since a wet floor under a flat mat is where trouble starts.

faq.q: Can a bath mat really be mildew resistant?
faq.a: Makers use the term, but no mat is immune. Mildew grows where moisture and soap film sit. A mat that drains well, dries quickly and is washed regularly resists mildew far better than a label can. A mat that is washed on schedule and hung after use rarely needs a stronger remedy, and in most households those two habits are all that is required.

faq.q: How do I stop mildew under a suction mat?
faq.a: Lift the mat after each shower, rinse both sides and hang it so air reaches the cups. Wash it every few weeks and wipe the tub floor. Keep the bathroom ventilated. If dark spots appear, a short soak in diluted white vinegar followed by a thorough cold rinse often lifts light mildew without harming the cups.

faq.q: What do the hooks on the homerella kids mat do?
faq.a: They are two self-adhesive hooks that let you hang the mat after each use. Hanging lets both sides dry, which is the most effective anti-mildew habit. Place them on a clean, dry wall. A bathroom without a window benefits from an extractor fan left running for a while after a shower, which pulls humid air out and helps every surface dry.

faq.q: Should I use bleach on a mildewed mat?
faq.a: Avoid it. Bleach can damage cups and materials and leave a film. Use a cold wash, a mild vinegar soak and a good rinse. If mildew returns quickly, replace the mat. If you notice a persistent musty smell even after washing, retire the mat, because mildew can lodge in material where washing cannot reach.

faq.q: How often should I wash a mat?
faq.a: A rinse after each shower and a machine wash every two to four weeks suits most households, more often in a humid bathroom. A musty smell means it is overdue. A mat that is left rolled up or folded while damp will bloom quickly, so always dry it open before storing.

faq.q: Does a hang-to-dry mat need a special wall?
faq.a: Adhesive hooks need a clean, smooth, dry surface and a cure time. If your wall is textured, use a towel bar or the tub edge. Test the hold before hanging a wet mat. Rinsing the tub floor after a bath also helps, because soap scum on the floor feeds mildew just as it does on the mat. In a rental, ask about ventilation if mildew keeps returning, since a fan or window can solve more than any mat can.
